about: The wind: which plate each shot's strips fly over, which way the wind blows (toward the lens or away from it), and the few strips that pass close enough to read. A hero strip's keys are [frame, x, y, z] in metres from the lens (x right, y down, z into the hall). Every text here is in the plan's source table: three short dated quotations in quotation marks, and two common sayings without them. B08 is the macro of one strip in her fingers: the type is laid along the strip found in each frame. A shot may list several plates in a row (a cut inside the shot). Each plate says where its vanishing point is (vanish), the column she stands in (figure: x0, x1, y0, and optionally how dark counts as her) and how far she is from the lens (depth), so strips and smoke beyond her pass behind her. smoke adds wind-tunnel ribbons that converge on the vanishing point.

heroes.text: “FROM ONE MILLION TO TEN MILLION YEARS.”

B04.was: until v012 each strip was in reach of the eye for 8 or 9 frames, one after the other, either side of the cut inside the shot. Review found that they passed too fast to read. Each now arrives in two or three frames and hangs, drifting slowly toward the lens, for 20 to 24 frames, and the two overlap; they ride across the cut inside the shot as the camera does.

B06.was: until v012 the three strips came one after another, each readable for about 7 frames. They now overlap, each in its own part of the frame, and each hangs for 16 to 21 frames.

B08.was: until the sixth pass: a narrow strip (drafts/macro_hands.mp4, in 1.0, zoom 1.5, dx 0.06, dy 0.02, type along [0.22, 0.70]); her reel shows a card, so the macro now shows the card
